chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Khalid (who narrated from the one who told him), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He used to say: 'The one who enters the Ka'bah enters with Allah being pleased with him, and he exits free of sins.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic building in Mecca considered the holiest site in Islam
key_terms.رَاضٍ: Pleased or satisfied (referring to Allah's pleasure)
key_terms.عُطْلًا: Free, clear, or discharged (specifically of debts or sins)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of entering the Ka'bah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual efficacy of entering the Ka'bah, promising divine pleasure and the expulsion of sins for the visitor. This narration underscores the Ka'bah not merely as a physical structure but as a locus of spiritual purification, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of the House of God as a means of drawing closer to Allah.
